To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the microscopic spectral density of random matrix models at their critical point has a nontrivial scaling limit, which is in agreement with numerical results, and that similar sum rules may be expected to hold for QCD at its chiral transition.

the microscopic spectral density of random matrix models is expected to have the same scaling behavior near the critical point as in the chiral limit, and that the same scaling behavior is expected for QCD at the chiral critical point and at the chiral transition if it is amenable to an analysis based on Ginzburg-Ladua theory.
the inverse moments of eigenvalues in chiral random matrix ensembles scale with the inverse of the volume at the critical point, and the microscopic density is in agreement with numerical results.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the critical behaviour of QCD at finite temperature and density.
the critical scaling at zero virtuality of the QCD Dirac operator.
the study of the phase structure of quantum chromodynamics (QCD), and the associated phase transition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the critical point of a random matrix model with chiral symmetry has the property that the inverse moments of its microscopic eigenvalues scale as a power of the inverse temperature.
, at the critical point, the microscopic spectral density of random matrix models is a smooth function of the energy.

, in the vicinity of a second order phase transition, the microscopic spectral density of the QCD Dirac operator is given by a universal function which is a solution of the microscopic spectral density equation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the critical scaling of the moments of eigenvalues at zero virtuality is a general feature of the critical points of chiral random matrices, and that this is expected to hold also in the QCD critical point.
we have found a new type of universality in the chiral transition, that is not present for the usual random matrix models.
at the critical temperature the QCD spectrum is expected to be characterized by a universal critical scaling law, and a universal critical scaling function.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the critical scaling laws for QCD are different from those in the conventional random matrix ensembles, and that they can be used for a critical analysis of the chiral transition in the continuum limit.
, in a certain sense, criticality at zero temperature is more accessible than at zero chemical potential.
the chiral transition is not a phase transition in the usual sense, but rather a critical point.
